newsitem.title: DUBAI: Gulf allies meet on Qatar-Bahrain dispute.
newsitem.headline: Gulf allies meet on Qatar-Bahrain dispute.

text.p: A committee of Gulf Arab foreign ministers set up to settle a border row between Bahrain and Qatar held its first meeting in Saudi Arabia on Tuesday, officials said.

They said the foreign ministers of Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, Oman and the United Arab Emirates met in the capital Riyadh in the first meeting of the committee set up in December by the six-nation Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC), which also groups Bahrain and Qatar.
The foreign ministers of Bahrain and Qatar were due to join the other ministers later on Tuesday for face-to-face talks on the dispute.

The committee was scheduled to hold its first meeting in Cairo last month on the sidelines of a conference of the Damascus Declaration grouping the GCC states, Syria and Egypt. But it was rescheduled at Saudi Arabia's request.
Qatar and Bahrain have for decades been locked in a dispute over a cluster of islands, sandbanks and reefs in the Gulf controlled by Bahrain since the 1930s but also claimed by Qatar.
Qatar has taken the case to the International Court of Justice at The Hague, a move bitterly opposed by Bahrain which insists on an Arab solution.
Ties worsened further after Bahrain put on trial two Qataris spying and boycotted a GCC summit in December to protest against Qatar's refusal to withdraw the case from The Hague.
Bahrain last month pardoned the two Qataris after a state security court sentenced them to three years in jail for spying.
